title: Slack Team Messaging: Complete Architecture
description: Design an enterprise team messaging platform with multi-tenant workspaces, channels, thread trees, WebSocket fan-out, and Flannel edge caching.

data.text: Design an enterprise-grade real-time collaboration and team messaging platform like Slack. The system supports multi-tenant workspaces with hundreds of thousands of concurrent users organized into public and private channels, direct messages, and hierarchical message threads. The primary technical hurdle is channel fan-out: broadcasting a message in a channel with 50,000 active members in under 100ms, maintaining unread badges and cursors, delivering real-time typing/presence signals, and providing sub-second search over years of workspace chat history.

terms.definition: Slack's custom edge caching proxy that terminates client WebSockets, caches channel membership and metadata, and multiplexes server traffic.
The mechanism of replicating a single incoming message across thousands of connected user WebSocket sessions subscribed to that channel.
A timestamp or message ID tracking the highest message seen by a user in a channel, used to compute unread counts.
A nested conversation model where child replies reference a root parent message without spamming the main channel stream.
A horizontal scaling system for MySQL used to shard workspace channels, messages, and membership lists by workspace ID.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Multi-tenant Workspaces & Channels: Public, private, and cross-organization shared channels (Slack Connect)
Real-time Messaging: Text, rich formatting, custom emojis, mentions (@user, @channel, @here), and file attachments
Threaded Conversations: Reply to specific messages in threads with optional "also send to channel" broadcasting
Presence & Typing Indicators: Real-time active/away/DND status and live "User is typing..." indicators
Unread & Badge Management: Accurate unread counters, mention badges, and cross-device read state synchronization
Full-Text Search: Search across channels, messages, snippets, and files with date and sender filters

data.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items: Scale: 30+ million daily active users; 100,000+ members in single enterprise workspaces; 1B+ messages/day
Delivery Latency: Sub-100ms message delivery to online members in channels with up to 50,000 subscribers
Availability: 99.99% uptime for core messaging and WebSocket connectivity
Data Integrity: Zero lost messages; strict chronological ordering within any single channel
Multi-device Synchronization: Read state and typing notifications sync instantaneously across web, desktop, and mobile

data.text: Slack isolates organizations by Workspace. WebSocket connections terminate at an edge proxy layer (Flannel/Envoy). Messages are published to an event bus (Kafka), persisted into sharded MySQL clusters (Vitess), and fanned out through Redis Pub/Sub to edge connection servers holding active subscriber sockets.

data.text: When a user posts in a large channel (e.g. #general with 20,000 members), broadcasting 20,000 messages directly from one server causes CPU and network choking. Slack solves this using Pub/Sub channel multiplexing at the Flannel edge.

data.caption: Message posting sequence with multiplexed Flannel edge fan-out and async push for offline members
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor Alice as 👤 Alice (Sender)
    participant EdgeA as 🌍 Flannel Edge A
    participant Ingest as ✉️ Ingest Service
    participant DB as 💬 Vitess MySQL
    participant PubSub as ⚡ Redis Pub/Sub
    participant EdgeB as 🌍 Flannel Edge B
    actor Bob as 👤 Bob (Online Member)
    participant Kafka as 📨 Kafka
    participant Push as 🔔 Push Worker
    actor Charlie as 👤 Charlie (Offline Member)

    Alice->>EdgeA: SendMessage(Channel: #general, "All-Hands starting!")
    EdgeA->>Ingest: POST /channel/message
    Ingest->>DB: INSERT Message (ChannelID, Timestamp, MsgID)
    DB-->>Ingest: OK (Committed)
    Ingest-->>EdgeA: Message Ack
    EdgeA-->>Alice: Render message locally (Delivered)

    par Real-time Push to Online Subscribers
        Ingest->>PubSub: PUBLISH channel:#general {msg_payload}
        PubSub->>EdgeB: Broadcast to Edge B (hosts Bob's socket)
        EdgeB->>Bob: Push message over WebSocket (<50ms)
    and Async Processing & Offline Push
        Ingest->>Kafka: Publish "MessageCreated" Event
        Kafka->>Push: Identify offline channel members
        Push->>Charlie: Send FCM/APNs Push Notification ("Alice in #general: All-Hands...")
    end

rows: Enterprise organizations with massive channels (50k+ members)
Multi-tenant Workspaces with isolated RBAC and channel scopes
Ephemeral server storage (deleted upon delivery, stored on client SQLite)
Permanent server history (cloud archive, search compliance, audit logs)
TLS in transit, encryption at rest with enterprise key management (EKM)
Distributed Elasticsearch clusters searching petabytes of history per company

faqs.question: How does Flannel reduce WebSocket connection memory and server load?
faqs.answer: In large workspaces, each client needs channel membership lists, user profiles, and channel states. Flannel sits at the edge and caches workspace metadata locally in RAM. When a client connects, Flannel provides the initial state bootstrap from its local cache, reducing database read storms by over 90% during morning peak login hours.

faqs.question: How are unread counts and read cursors computed without writing on every read?
faqs.answer: Each member has a `channel_last_read` table storing `(user_id, channel_id, last_read_message_id)`. When a user views a channel, their client throttles cursor updates (e.g. at most once every 5 seconds) and writes the latest message ID. The unread count is computed as `COUNT(messages WHERE channel_id = X AND message_id > last_read_message_id)`.

faqs.question: How does Slack guarantee strict message ordering within a channel?
faqs.answer: Messages within a channel must never appear out of order. Channels are sharded such that all messages for a specific `channel_id` map to the same Vitess database shard. Auto-incrementing 64-bit integer IDs or monotonic timestamps assigned by the primary shard database establish the definitive ordering.

faqs.question: How does Slack handle mentions (@channel, @here, @user)?
faqs.answer: When a message arrives, the Mention Service parses the text. If `@channel` is detected, it queries the channel membership set. For active members, an urgent notification event is emitted; for offline members, a push notification is dispatched. High-impact mentions in large channels (>1,000 members) prompt a confirmation modal to prevent accidental broadcast storms.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Flannel edge caching terminates client WebSockets and eliminates database bootstrap storms
Sharded MySQL (Vitess) partitions messages by Workspace and Channel ID for strict ordering
Pub/Sub broadcast through Redis delivers channel messages to online edge connections in <50ms
Read cursors track the highest read message ID to calculate unread badge counters efficiently
Asynchronous Kafka consumers decouple full-text search indexing and mobile push notifications
data.takeaway: Slack's high-concurrency architecture tackles enterprise-scale collaboration through multi-tenant data sharding, intelligent edge caching (Flannel), and lightweight message fan-out for channels with tens of thousands of members.
